title: Regulated tiered burst quota orchestration and emergency degradation playbook
creator: Marco Liu
description: Problem: During cross-region demand spikes we observe uneven burst absorption: some tenants drain global credits rapidly while others starve, and limiter control-plane outages cause abrupt fail-open behavior that violates SLOs. Goals: 1) define a deterministic, observable orchestration for tiered burst credits that preserves tenant fairness and SLOs across regions; 2) implement an emergency degradation mode (soft-shed + probabilistic admission) that keeps tail latency bounded when the control-plane is impaired; 3) produce an operational playbook and canary runbook for safe rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Tiered burst credit allocator implemented with deterministic proportional draining across regions
Degradation mode available: soft-shed with p95 latency SLO preserved for P0/P1 tenants and best-effort for P2/P3
Automated smoke tests that simulate limiter-control outage and verify graceful degradation behavior
Playbook published in Confluence with runbook steps, escalation contacts, and rollback instructions
Telemetry added: per-tenant effective-rate, credit-balance, admission-probability, and degradation-trigger events visible in Console
technical_notes: Design uses local ephemeral reservoirs per-edge to allow short bursts without immediate global lease negotiation
Global coordinator runs lease reconciliation every 5s; during unreachable coordinator windows edges switch to deterministic proportional drain using last-known weight vector
Admission during degradation uses a two-tier probabilistic policy: 100% accept for P0 until local cap, 75% for P1, 40% for P2, 10% for P3 with exponential backoff per-tenant when rejections observed
KV-cache keys include tenant_id, region, last_lease_ts to allow audit and postmortem reconstruction
Trade-off: shorter reconciliation window reduces overcommit risk but increases control-plane load; we default to 5s with A/B test to 3s for small tenants
Safety: include a hard global kill-switch that forces strict per-tenant rate limits even during coordinator lag (used only by SRE as part of escalation)
